title: Invariant and coinvariant sequence for native derived morphisms
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], $P:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ an additive exact autoequivalence, $\mathcal B=\mathcal A^P$ the fixed-pair category [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], and $U$ the forgetful functor. Use ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $M,N\in D(\mathcal B)$ with bounded cohomology put
$$V^r_{M,N}=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(D(U)M,D(U)N[r]),\qquad T^r(u)=\theta_{N[r]}D(P)(u)\theta_M^{-1}.$$
Here $\theta$ is the isomorphism induced by the termwise structure maps, with the canonical shift comparison. Define $(V^r)^T=\ker(1-T^r)$ and $(V^r)_T=\operatorname{coker}(1-T^r)$ as abelian groups. There is a natural short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow(V^{-1}_{M,N})_T\xrightarrow{\partial}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal B)}(M,N)\xrightarrow{D(U)}(V^0_{M,N})^T\longrightarrow0.$$
The right arrow is forgetting the action. The left arrow is the connecting map from the two-term free-action resolution, equivalently the class obtained by changing the action by an off-diagonal morphism into $N[-1]$ in a cone representative. The sequence is natural under precomposition and postcomposition by morphisms in $D(\mathcal B)$ and their underlying morphisms.

It is also natural for the following functors and for finite composites of them, on pairs whose images still have bounded cohomology. Let $\mathcal A'$ be Grothendieck abelian with an additive exact autoequivalence $P'$, fixed-pair category $\mathcal B'$ and forgetful functor $U'$, let $H:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$ be additive with a natural isomorphism $a:P'H\xrightarrow{\sim}HP$, and let $H^{\mathrm{eq}}(M,\theta)=(HM,H(\theta)a_M)$. If $H$ is exact, use the termwise functor $D(H^{\mathrm{eq}})$ with $D(U')D(H^{\mathrm{eq}})=D(H)D(U)$. If $H$ is left exact, use the total right derived functor $RH^{\mathrm{eq}}$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] with the canonical comparison $D(U')RH^{\mathrm{eq}}\cong RH\,D(U)$ of [lem-sf-fixed-pair-derived-forget-comparison], which is the identity of $H(UI)$ on K-injective complexes $I$. On both outer terms the map is induced by the underlying functor $D(H)$, resp. $RH$, its shift comparison and this comparison. Thus these functors preserve the displayed connecting map $\partial$, not merely the right-hand forgetting map. No assertion that forgetting is faithful on derived morphisms is made.

proof.text: Raw naturality gives naturality of the descended family on quotient representatives. A normalized off-diagonal SES is a presentation with identity endpoint isomorphisms, so the presentation equality computes its boundary exactly. For any other normalized natural family, transport a strict presentation along its endpoint isomorphisms, using boundedness invariance under isomorphism. This computes its value on every quotient representative and proves uniqueness.

proof.text: For the exact companion, additivity of transport follows directly from additivity of D(L) and bilinearity of composition. The exact action lemma gives T-compatibility. Naturality of alpha and the coherent zero-shift equation prove the forgetting square. Present each u using the raw off-diagonal boundary, and compute the source normalized boundary on that presentation. Map the presentation by the exact-presentation lemma, then compute the target normalized boundary on it. The two normalized-presentation evaluations give the boundary square. This four-clause assembly is implemented in Lean; the right-derived and finite-composite companions are assembled in the following steps.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-exact-input-derived-transformation] with exact input the identity and beta the identity unitor to obtain unit-compatible shifts and triangulatedness for each recorded right-derived functor. Triangulatedness implies additivity. The transport_additive and transport_forget calculations then give the additive and forgetting clauses without any action-specific theorem. Apply [lem-sf-cyclic-derived-right-action] for the T-clause. Present u using [lem-sf-cyclic-derived-off-diagonal-presentation], transport that presentation using [lem-sf-cyclic-derived-right-presentation], and evaluate both normalized boundaries by normalized_boundary_on_presentation. This proves the right-derived four-clause theorem.

For a composite, expand map_comp and the composite shift comparison, and use naturality of the second shift comparison at the first inverse forgetting comparison. proof.text: Induct on Generated. Each underlying generator is additive: exact functors by localization and right derived functors by the unit-compatible triangulatedness supplied above. Prove two identities simultaneously at every native pair, without bounds: transport commutes with T, and native functoriality commutes with the raw off-diagonal boundary. For exact generators use [lem-sf-cyclic-derived-exact-action] and [lem-sf-cyclic-derived-exact-presentation]; for right-derived generators use [lem-sf-cyclic-derived-right-action] and [lem-sf-cyclic-derived-right-presentation], with the unit-compatible underlying shift supplied in Generated. The identity case follows from identity transport. Paste both identities at a composite using the proved transport composition equality and functoriality. Finally evaluate the raw boundaries at the bounded source and final target using their strict presentations and normalized_boundary_on_presentation. Together with additivity and the general forgetting calculation this proves finite-composite functoriality with no intermediate bound assumption.
